summary: Covers path reoptimization for loosely routed point-to-multipoint traffic engineering LSPs in RSVP-TE. It applies existing point-to-point reoptimization mechanisms, identifies the problems, and defines procedures to address them. This includes handling many sub-LSPs in one tree.

plainLanguage.summary: If a delivery truck's route to many houses can be improved, you want to switch without losing packages. This explains how to do that for a whole tree of routes.

questions: what is p2mp te lsp reoptimization
what is preferable p2mp-te tree exists
subtitle: New RSVP-TE signaling so a multicast tree of loosely routed paths can be reoptimized as a whole, even when messages are split into fragments.

tldr.problem: Existing reoptimization for loosely routed point-to-point LSPs does not cleanly extend to a point-to-multipoint tree, where it can trigger premature partial reoptimization, and fragmented RSVP messages can arrive out of order with no clear start and end.
tldr.mechanism: It defines a Tree Re-evaluation Request flag, a Preferable P2MP-TE Tree Exists PathErr sub-code, and an S2L_SUB_LSP_FRAG object that numbers the fragments of a sub-LSP descriptor list.
tldr.outcome: The ingress node can request and learn about whole-tree reoptimization, and receivers can rebuild fragmented sub-LSP lists unambiguously.

facts.label: Tree re-evaluation flag
facts.value: Bit 14 in the Attribute Flags TLV

today: RFC 8149 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFCs. It builds on RFC 4736 and RFC 4875.

sections.title: Reoptimizing Loosely Routed P2MP Trees
sections.content:
A P2MP-TE LSP is made of one or more source-to-leaf (S2L) sub-LSPs. A sub-LSP is loosely routed if its path is not fully spelled out by the ingress node when it is signaled: there is no Explicit Route Object (ERO), the ERO has a loose next hop, or it has an abstract node that identifies more than one node. This is common for inter-domain trees where no Path Computation Element is used.

RFC 4875 lets an ingress node reoptimize the whole tree with make-before-break (MBB), or reoptimize one or a set of sub-LSPs using the Sub-Group-based method. RFC 4736 defines reoptimization for loosely routed point-to-point LSPs. This document applies those mechanisms to P2MP trees, finds the problems, and fixes them.
sections.plainLanguage: A tree of routes to many places is built from many small paths. Some bends in those paths are not decided in advance, and this RFC helps improve the whole tree when a better one exists.

sections.title: What RFC 4736 Already Does
sections.content:
For point-to-point LSPs, a midpoint LSR that expands loose next hops sends a PathErr with Notify error code 25 and sub-code 6 ("Preferable Path Exists"). The ingress node can ask midpoints to re-evaluate by setting the "Path Re-evaluation Request" flag (0x20) in the SESSION_ATTRIBUTES object of the Path message. On receiving the PathErr, the ingress node reoptimizes with MBB using a different LSP-ID.

Applied to a P2MP tree, this means sending requests and PathErrs for all S2L sub-LSPs, typically hundreds. Midpoints might have to wait with a timer to treat these as one tree request, ingress nodes must guess whether to reoptimize the tree or a subset, and acting on a subset early can cause data duplication that reoptimizing the whole tree would avoid.

Combining sub-LSPs in one message with a descriptor list does not fully fix this. Branching LSRs split the list, so a PathErr may name only a subset and the ingress node cannot tell whether to use same-LSP-ID sub-group reoptimization or different-LSP-ID tree reoptimization.
sections.plainLanguage: The old way works for one route, but for a whole tree it means hundreds of notes that may arrive in pieces. The ingress is left guessing whether to fix one branch or the whole tree.

sections.title: Tree-Based Reoptimization
sections.content:
To evaluate the tree, an ingress node MAY send a Path message with the new P2MP-TE Tree Re-evaluation Request flag set, bit number 14 in the Attribute Flags TLV. It selects one sub-LSP transiting each midpoint to carry the request and MAY send it to each border LSR on the tree.

A midpoint LSR that expands loose next hops MUST re-evaluate all the sub-LSPs that are expansions of those loose hops. If it finds a preferable tree, it MUST send a PathErr with Notify error code 25 and the new sub-code 13, "Preferable P2MP-TE Tree Exists", and SHOULD NOT propagate the flag downstream. If it finds none, it MUST propagate the request downstream by setting the flag in the LSP_ATTRIBUTES object of the Path message.

A midpoint MAY also send this PathErr unsolicited, and SHOULD consider how often to do so because the PathErr may be lost or ignored. When the ingress node receives it, it SHOULD reoptimize the LSP using MBB with a different LSP-ID.
sections.plainLanguage: The ingress can ask each stop along the way, is there a better whole tree? A stop that finds one says so, and otherwise passes the question along.

sections.title: Fragment Identifier Object
sections.content:
Large descriptor lists may have to be semantically fragmented, and fragments can arrive out of order. The new S2L_SUB_LSP_FRAG object (Class Number 204, C-Type 1, length 8 bytes) lets receivers rebuild the list. It is placed before the S2L_SUB_LSP object in each fragmented descriptor.

  • Fragment ID: 16 bits, 1 to 65535, incremented for each new message that needs fragmenting and reset to 1 after 65535. Its scope is limited to the RSVP message type, so Path and PathErr do not correlate.
  • Fragments Total: 8 bits, 1 to 255, the same in all fragments with a common fragment ID.
  • Fragment Number: 8 bits, 1 to 255, the position of this fragment.
sections.plainLanguage: When a long list is split across several envelopes, each gets a label such as 2 of 5, so the reader can put them back in order.

sections.title: Sub-Group Reoptimization with Fragments
sections.content:
The new object is optional, with two exceptions. If an LSR semantically fragments a Path message because the descriptor list does not fit, it MUST add the fragment object to each fragment. In any other situation where an RSVP message must be fragmented, it MUST also add it.

A midpoint LSR that receives a re-evaluation request with the fragment object SHOULD wait to collect all sub-LSPs before re-evaluating. If fragments are not all received within a configurable interval, it SHOULD trigger re-evaluation of all sub-LSPs of the P2MP-TE LSP transiting the node, provided it received at least one fragment.

An ingress node behaves similarly with fragmented PathErr messages carrying the "Preferable Path Exists" sub-code: it SHOULD wait for all fragments, and after the configurable interval SHOULD reoptimize all sub-LSPs of the tree transiting the midpoint that sent the PathErr, provided it received at least one fragment.
sections.plainLanguage: The receiver waits for all numbered pieces. If some never come, it plays it safe and rechecks everything from that sender.

sections.title: Compatibility and Registrations
sections.content:
Both new elements are designed so that nodes not supporting them are unaffected. LSP_ATTRIBUTES and the new fragment object use class numbers of the form 11bbbbbb, so under RFC 2205 a non-supporting node ignores the new flag or object and forwards it unchanged.

IANA registered bit 14 in the Attribute Flags registry (valid in Path, not in Resv, RRO or ERO), sub-code 13 under Notify error code 25, and Class Number 204 (S2L_SUB_LSP_FRAG) with C-Type 1.
sections.plainLanguage: Older routers that do not know the new labels just pass them along without reading them, so nothing breaks.
